case_name: Zonal Manager, Central Bank Of India v M/S Devi Ispat Ltd. & Ors.
petitioner: Zonal Manager, Central Bank Of India
facts: The Respondent-Company carries on the business of manufacturing and trading in ingots and various other types of steel and for the said purpose requires financial support from the institution like the appellant-Bank.
On 16.10.2006, the respondent-Company wrote to the appellant-Bank requesting it to review and enhance its credit facilities.
The Bank advised the Company to shift its borrowings to some other Bank due to certain irregularities in the accounts of the respondent-Company.
The Company requested the Bank to return the title deeds and other collateral securities to enable them to entrust the same to other Nationalized Bank.
issues: Whether the direction of the learned single Judge affirmed by the Division Bench for return of the title deeds deposited by the respondent-Company as a security can be a subject-matter of Art. 226 of the Constitution of India.
Whether the writ petition before the High Court under Art. 226 is maintainable and the High Court is fully justified in issuing direction for return of the title deeds of the Company.
petitioner_arguments: The direction of the learned single Judge affirmed by the Division Bench for return of the title deeds deposited by the respondent-Company as a security cannot be a subject-matter of Art. 226 of the Constitution of India.
Right to retain a mortgage deed is a civil dispute and proper forum is Debts Recovery Tribunal (in short 'DRT') or civil court.
respondent_arguments: The writ petition before the High Court under Art. 226 is maintainable and the High Court is fully justified in issuing direction for return of the title deeds of the Company.

The respondent-Company carries on the business of manufacturing and trading in ingots and various other types of steel and for the said purpose, it requires financial support from the institution like the appellant-Bank.
court_reasoning: It is true that the respondent-Company filed a writ petition before the learned single Judge of the Calcutta High Court praying for issuance of a writ of mandamus directing the Bank to forthwith take steps to release the security documents and issue 'NOC' and 'NDC' pertaining to their company's accounts without any further delay.

The respondent-Company had cleared the dues which were pending at the relevant point of time through the State Bank of India, they are entitled to get their title deeds to enable them to deposit the same with the State Bank of India as their security for the amount advanced.
holding: The High Court dismissed the appeal filed by the appellant-Bank and directed the Bank to return forthwith the title deeds deposited by M/s Devi Ispat Ltd., the Respondent-Company herein.
